description: §17.7.3 — a `let` declaration inside an `<each>` body interpolation (`${ let nm = @.name }`) fires E-EACH-BODY-DECL-UNSUPPORTED (fail-closed, S339-peter). Pre-fix the decl was silently DROPPED while a later `${nm}` lowered to a dangling `String(nm)` → the whole list rendered empty at exit-0 with no diagnostic. The each-body scope is the `@.` sigil + optional `as` alias, not author-declared locals.
rationale: §17.7.3: the each-body scope is the `@.` contextual sigil plus an optional `as` alias; author-declared locals are not part of it. Silently dropping the decl while still emitting a reference to it is a miscompile (dangling ref → empty render, exit-0, no diagnostic). The compiler rejects the unsupported form loudly (fail-closed) rather than ship a silently-broken bundle; SUPPORTING author locals (replay the binding into the per-item factory) is a separate §17.7.3 language-surface ruling this row does not pre-decide.
